meta.expect: No deal while none of her points has been answered

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in class. Who decided that?
Thanks for coming in. So, the AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%, which is pretty conclusive, so that's why he got the zero.
Pretty conclusive. That's a machine's guess, and the people who sell these tools say in print never to punish a student on the score alone. What else do you have?

Let me back up, because I started in the wrong place. I entered the zero on November 3 before calling you. Your printed procedure, 4.2, says I should have called first. That was wrong, and Owen should not have found out on his phone in class.
Okay. Keep going.

I'll set the checker aside; it's my weakest piece. I've turned my screen to you: this is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM, with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of small edits to font, name and spacing. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. He told me he wrote it over the weekend, so that's a boy pasting in his own draft. Is there anything that says otherwise?

If he drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in, it would look like that too, so here is something you can check yourself. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the play open to 3.2. Look for it.
Seventeen-year-olds misquote things. Whatever comes of this, it stays off his record and it stays quiet. Is that understood, Hale?
And here is his outline from October 15, which he handed in himself. It argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay. That's called thinking. And you skipped my question about his record.

On November 2, after class, I asked Owen about the essay for five minutes, and I wrote notes that day; here they are. Asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck." He couldn't say which scene his second paragraph was about. And here is his in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.
Five minutes after class, with a teenager put on the spot, is not a hearing. Send me the version history, printed, with those times on it.

I'm not asking you to say Owen cheated. Here's what I'm offering under procedure 4.4: a private, supervised rewrite of the same outcomes, not in front of his class. Its mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Fine. He'll sit it to put this behind him, not because he did anything. I want that in writing tonight, and the mark entered before December 1.
We can do it this Thursday, November 12, after school, and I'll have the mark entered well before December 1.
Okay. Thursday. And there is nothing on his record right now, Hale?
Do we have an agreement?
Answer my question first.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Hale,

You agreed today to a private, supervised rewrite of Owen's Hamlet essay under procedure 4.4 on Thursday, November 12, after school, not in front of his class, with its mark replacing the zero, the mark entered before December 1, and nothing placed on his record. I still require your written confirmation that nothing is on Owen's record right now, along with the printed version history you showed me. I expect all of this in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Last position: she agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday after school and still wants your written commitment tonight plus confirmation that nothing is on his record now; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4.
What moved her: You answered her pasted-draft defence with a misquoted line she could check in the play herself, which let the version history stand as evidence she couldn't wave away.
What cost ground: You opened with the checker score and called it conclusive, which handed her the false-positive argument she came armed with and delayed everything else.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history placed the whole essay in the late hours of October 28, the night before it was due, which was very close to that memory; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked whether anything was on his record right now, answer that plainly before asking if you have an agreement, because it was the one thing she would not let go.
